answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence depends on paths reaching independently vouched regions, not on self-issued identities. When voting weight is derived from walk mass, a sybil cluster joined to the honest graph by a sparse external cut has low conductance; spectral and min-cut bounds limit walks entering it and thus cap its aggregate weight. Cedar, vine, and jade label distinct attestations, not additional votes.
